leadIn.title: Lead-In & Context: Intensifiers
leadIn.content: Modifying strength: It is very cold outside today, but yesterday it was extremely cold. This shirt is quite nice.

meaningCheck.question: "Intensifiers" — Does the condition describe a real possibility or a hypothetical imaginary scenario?
options: It sets up a specific condition and its communicative result
It describes a guaranteed past fact that cannot change
It is only used for giving formal orders
meaningCheck.explanation: Correct · Conditionals express dependent conditions and their logical outcomes.

meaningCheck.question: Structural check: In conditional sentences, can the 'if' clause come second?
options: No, the 'if' clause must always be the first two words
Yes, clause order can flip without changing the fundamental condition
meaningCheck.explanation: Correct · Clause position can reverse; a comma is used when 'if' starts the sentence.

form.title: Form & Structure: Intensifiers
form.content: Very / Really / Extremely / Quite + adjective or adverb (e.g. very fast, really happy, quite good).

pronunciation.title: Pronunciation Notes: Intensifiers
pronunciation.content: Spoken stress, weak forms, intonation, and articulation patterns for Intensifiers.

controlledPractice.question: 'This soup is ___ salty for me.' (a problem)
controlledPractice.explanation: Too signals more than wanted · a problem.

controlledPractice.question: 'It's really good!' means:
controlledPractice.explanation: Really strengthens a positive meaning, with no problem implied.

controlledPractice.question: Which is the mildest intensifier?
controlledPractice.explanation: Quite sits in the medium range on the intensity scale.
